facts.fact: Home Affairs provincial managers told the Portfolio Committee that births are registered at connected health facilities by Home Affairs officials posted or roaming there, and at Wesfleur Hospital in place of the closed Atlantis office; the passages name no digital registration of deaths, and give no meeting date, so the document's published date is used.
facts.system: birth registration at connected health facilities

facts.fact: The KwaZulu-Natal provincial manager of Home Affairs said the province has 47 connected health facilities for birth registration, covered by 13 permanent officials and one roaming official per district across five districts; this is one province's count, with no national total, and the Eastern Cape separately reported 23 health facilities assisting with birth registration without saying they are connected; the document's published date is used.
facts.system: birth registration at connected health facilities

facts.fact: Birth registration at connected health facilities is staffed by Home Affairs officials, and the Department's Deputy Director-General for Civic Services said the Department is itself working to automate birth registration and, with the Department of Health, to connect more health facilities; the document's published date is used.
facts.system: birth registration at connected health facilities

Also stated: some KwaZulu-Natal health facilities have limited or no permanent staff, which delays registration; hospital clerk posts for birth registration were never created or funded there; the Director-General said rural areas would still need mobile services; Eastern Cape holds 4,871 late birth registration applications.
